system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Retinitis pigmentosa with preferential early rod photoreceptor degeneration
mechanism: Retinitis pigmentosa is a genetically heterogeneous group of inherited retinal dystrophies. In the typical rod-cone form, rod photoreceptors are preferentially affected early. Progressive rod dysfunction causes nyctalopia and peripheral visual-field loss; cone dysfunction develops later and can impair color and central vision. Retinal pigment epithelium becomes secondarily abnormal, and migrating pigment-containing cells contribute to the characteristic bone-spicule fundus appearance.
vignette: A 22-year-old man reports several years of progressively worsening vision in dim light. He now frequently bumps into objects approaching from either side but can still read small print in good lighting. Funduscopic examination shows bilateral midperipheral bone-spicule pigmentation and attenuated retinal vessels. There is no ocular pain or acute change in vision.
lead: In the typical form of this disorder, which of the following retinal cell populations is preferentially affected early in the disease process?
distractor_notes: Cone dysfunction can occur later in retinitis pigmentosa and contributes to impaired color discrimination and central visual loss. The early combination of nyctalopia and peripheral-field constriction reflects preferential rod dysfunction.

Retinal pigment epithelium becomes abnormal as photoreceptor degeneration progresses, and pigment migration contributes to bone-spicule deposits. In the typical rod-cone form, the primary early photoreceptor loss is rod-predominant.
Retinal ganglion cells are output neurons whose axons form the optic nerve; they are not the preferentially affected early photoreceptor population in typical retinitis pigmentosa.

Bipolar cells relay signals from photoreceptors to inner retinal neurons. The characteristic early defect in typical retinitis pigmentosa is degeneration of rods rather than preferential primary bipolar-cell loss.
key_expl: This patient has classic retinitis pigmentosa: progressive night blindness followed by peripheral visual-field constriction with bone-spicule retinal pigmentation. In the typical rod-cone form, genetic defects preferentially impair rod photoreceptors early. Because rods mediate scotopic vision and are concentrated outside the fovea, rod loss produces nyctalopia and progressive peripheral-field loss before central cone-mediated vision is substantially affected. Cone and retinal pigment epithelial abnormalities become more prominent later.
objective: Explain why typical retinitis pigmentosa first causes night blindness and peripheral-field loss by linking the phenotype to preferential early degeneration of rod photoreceptors.
